comments.author: hnrodey
comments.story: Many popular websites see what you type before you hit submit
comments.why: Early Instagram silently uploaded photos before posting to feel instant
comments.text: In the early days, Instagram silently uploaded your photo before you actually officially posted as a way to improve the "speed" of the user experience. So go ahead and add your filters, the text for the post, etc. because then the moment you clicked Post the app presented like it happened immediately. All for the UX. Source: Kevin Systrom on Lex Fridman Podcast [VIDEO]

comments.author: BoumTAC
comments.why: Instagram scaled to 50 million users on Django with a small team
comments.text: I watch the other day, the Lex Fridman podcast with Kevin Systrom, founder of Instagram. He talks about the scaling issue; they were using Django at that time and scale up to 50 millions users with a small team of developers. I do not think a majority of companies have more than 50 millions users and absolutely need to go full microservices. [VIDEO]
